display_name: US NIST AI Risk Management Framework
summary: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) provides a voluntary, rights-preserving framework for managing risks associated with AI systems. It is structured around four core functions: Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage, enabling organizations to address AI risks throughout the system lifecycle.

risk_tiers.description: AI systems with risks that cannot be adequately mitigated and should not be deployed. Determined through the Map and Measure functions when residual risks exceed organizational tolerance.
criteria: AI systems where potential harms are catastrophic and irreversible
Systems that fundamentally undermine civil rights or democratic values
AI applications where no effective risk mitigation is feasible
Systems operating in safety-critical domains without adequate fail-safes

risk_tiers.description: AI systems with significant potential for adverse impacts on individuals, communities, or society. Requires comprehensive risk management across all four framework functions.
criteria: AI systems making consequential decisions about individuals (employment, credit, housing)
Systems deployed in safety-critical environments (healthcare, transportation, infrastructure)
AI with potential for significant bias or discrimination impacts
Systems processing sensitive personal data at scale
Autonomous systems with limited human oversight capability

risk_tiers.description: AI systems with moderate potential for adverse impacts that can be effectively managed through standard risk management practices and transparency measures.
criteria: AI systems with human-in-the-loop for consequential decisions
Content generation systems with appropriate disclosure
Recommendation systems with moderate individual impact
AI-assisted analytics with human review of outputs

risk_tiers.description: AI systems with negligible potential for adverse impacts. Basic governance practices and monitoring are sufficient.
criteria: Internal productivity tools with no external impact
AI systems with well-understood and bounded behavior
Low-stakes automation with easy human override
Research and development prototypes not deployed to production

key_obligations.obligation: Establish AI governance policies, processes, procedures, and practices across the organization including roles, responsibilities, and accountability structures (GOVERN function)
Categorize and contextualize AI systems to identify potential risks, including mapping intended and unintended impacts on individuals, communities, and ecosystems (MAP function)
Employ quantitative and qualitative methods to analyze, assess, benchmark, and monitor AI risk and related impacts using appropriate metrics and methodologies (MEASURE function)
Allocate risk management resources and implement plans to respond to, recover from, and communicate about AI risks and incidents (MANAGE function)
Ensure AI systems are valid, reliable, safe, secure, resilient, accountable, transparent, explainable, interpretable, privacy-enhanced, and fair with harmful bias managed
key_obligations.article_reference: AI RMF Characteristics of Trustworthy AI

key_obligations.obligation: Implement processes for ongoing monitoring, periodic evaluation, and continuous improvement of AI risk management practices

enforcement_timeline: Voluntary framework published January 2023. Executive Order 14110 (October 2023) directs federal agencies to adopt AI RMF. NIST AI RMF Playbook and profiles provide implementation guidance.
recent_changes: NIST AI RMF Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) released addressing generative AI-specific risks
Companion NIST AI RMF Playbook updated with practical implementation guidance
Crosswalks published mapping AI RMF to ISO/IEC 23894 and EU AI Act requirements
